goal: Identify competing theories of clathrin pit formation, published datasets that can distinguish them, and the minimum Mechanome capabilities needed for fair comparisons.
constraints: Existing Mechanome models and the cooperative-adaptor proposal are candidates, not established explanations.
Assess whether predictions can be distinguished by available measurements before substantial candidate-model implementation.
Keep a paper's theoretical interpretation separate from its experimental measurements.
Treat continuous and delayed curvature as trajectories that may emerge from the same mechanism.
Preserve claim-level provenance, assumptions, negative results, and unresolved reviewer objections.
Do not treat a solver failure or missing software capability as biological refutation.
Use an observation model for fluorescence, reconstructed geometry, and temporal trajectories.
Do not treat static population ordering as a measured single-pit trajectory.
No paid campaign or external commitments are authorized by this specification.
